answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, like light passing through a prism that reveals a single beam: one identity, one deposit. An attacker who spins up thousands of fake agents must fund every ivory-tower copy separately, so cost grows linearly while honest agents reuse one stake across many jobs. When fraud is proven, the stake is slashed, turning a cheap gale of fake identities into an expensive storm the attacker pays for.
